quick.summary: How to link your daily tasks to the way your company makes money.
quick.takeaway: Every item needs a clear reason why it helps the business.

beats.line: My list is full of cool ideas. But do they actually pay the bills?
Think of a coffee shop. What if they spent all day polishing the floor?
Clean floors are nice. But they sell coffee to make money.
Exactly. Your list needs to build what sells.
We call this strategic alignment in product development.
Can I just say making things that make money?
Perfect. Every item needs a clear reason why it helps the business.
So I ask how each feature gets new users or keeps old ones?
If you cannot answer that, do not build it.

quiz.question: How do you decide if a cool new idea belongs on your list?
options: Does it get or keep users?
Did a manager ask for it?
quiz.explanation: Ideas only belong on the list if they help the business succeed.

quiz.question: A great feature is worth building even if it does not help the business.
quiz.explanation: If it does not make money or keep users, it is just polishing the floor.
